questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Electromagnetic waves are not deflected by electric and magnetic field.

Statement II : The amplitude of electric field and the magnetic field in electromagnetic waves are& related to each other as& ${E}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu0}{ε0}}{B}_{0}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement-I is correct as Electromagnetic waves& are neutral.

Statement-II is wrong as

$c = \dfrac{E0}{B0} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{E0}{B0} ⇒ {E}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ε}_{0}}}{B}_{0}$

questions.q: The magnetic field vector of an electromagnetic wave is given by $B = {B}_{0}\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}cos  \left(kz - \omegat\right)$~where $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j}$ represents unit vector along $x$ and $y$-axis respectively. At $t = 0s,$~two electric charges ${q}_{1}$ of 4\picoulomb and ${q}_{2}$ of 2\picoulomb located at \left(0, 0, $\dfrac{π}{k}\right)and \left(0, 0, $\dfrac{3\pi}{k}\right),~respectively, have the same velocity of $0 . 5c\overset{^}{i},$~(where $c$ is the velocity of light ). The ratio of the force acting on charge ${q}_{1}$ to ${q}_{2} is :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At $t = 0$
$B$ at \left(0, 0, \dfrac{π}{k}\right) = {B}_{0} \left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\right)$cos\left(\pi\right)
$B$ at \left($0, 0, $\dfrac{3\pi}{k}\right) = {B}_{0} \left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\r$right)cos\l$left(3\pi\right)
Force on charged particle ${q}_{1}$
${F}_{1} = {q}_{1}\overset{→}{V}1 $\times \overset{→}{B}$1$
$= $4\pi \left(0 . 5c\overset{^}{i}\right)\times \left[- {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\right)\right] = \dfrac{4\pi{B}_{0}c}{2\sqrt{2}} \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)
Force on charged particle ${q}_{2}$
${F}_{2} = {q}_{2}\overset{→}{V}2 $\times \overset{→}{B}$2$
$= $2\pi \left($0 . 5c\overset{^}{i}\$right)\times \left[- {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\right)\right] = \dfrac{2\pi{B}_{0}c}{2\sqrt{2}} \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$⇒ $\dfrac{F1}{F2} =$2$

questions.q: The amplitude of magnetic field in an electromagnetic wave propagating along $y$-axis is $6 . 0 \times {10}^{– 7}T$. The maximum value of electric field in the electromagnetic wave is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between the electric field and magnetic field is given by

${E}_{0} = c{B}_{0}$.

The given data is~

${B}_{0} = 6 \times {10}^{- 7}T$

$c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$

Thus, the maximum value of the electric field is

${E}_{0} = \left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right) \times \left(6 \times {10}^{– 7}\right) = 180Vm^{- 1}$.

The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by
$\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}cos ⁡ \left(kz\right)cos ⁡ ( \omegat )$

$\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}\overset{^}{i}cos \left(kz\right)cos \left(\omegat\right)
$\overset{→}{E} = $\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{2}\overset{^}{i}$cos \left($kz - \omegat\right) + $\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{2}\overset{^}{i}$cos\left($kz + \omegat\right)$
$\overset{→}{B} = $\dfrac{E0}{2C}\overset{^}{j}$cos \left(kz - \omegat\right) + \dfrac{E0}{2C}\overset{^}{j}cos\left(kz + \omegat\right)$
$= \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{2C}\overset{^}{j} \left[$2sin \left(kz\right)sin \left(\omegat\right)\right]

questions.q: If Electric field intensity of a uniform plane electro magnetic wave is given as& $E = - 301 . 6sin\left(kz - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{a}x + 452 . 4sin\left(kz - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{a}yVm^{- 1} .$~Then, magnetic intensity $H$~of this wave in $Am^{- 1}$ will be [Given : Speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, Permeability of vacuum ${μ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}NA^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between magnetic field and electric field is given by,

$c = \dfrac{E0}{B0} ⇒ {B}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{c}$

And magnetic intensity is given by,

${H}_{0} = \dfrac{B0}{\mu0} ⇒ {H}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{c{μ}_{0}}$

Also,~$\overset{→}{E}$~and~$\overset{→}{B}$~are perpendicular to each other.

Therefore,

\left|{H}_{y0}\right| = \dfrac{301 . 6}{3 \times {10}^{8} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}} = 0 . 8Am^{- 1}\left|{H}_{x0}\right| = \dfrac{452 . 4}{3 \times {10}^{8} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}} = 1 . 2Am^{- 1}$

Hence, C is the answer.

$

questions.q: Due to presence of an em-wave whose electric component is given by $\mathrm{E}=100 \sin (\omega \mathrm{t}-\mathrm{kx}) \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$, a cylinder of length 200 cm holds certain amount of em-energy inside it. If another cylinder of same length but half diameter than previous one holds same amount of em-energy, the magnitude of the electric field of the corresponding em-wave should be modified as
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy density of an $E M_{\text {wave }}=\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon E_0^2$, whare $E_0$ is the amplitude of the wave.
Since total energy is same for both cylinders
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon E_1^2\right) \pi R_1^2 L_1=\left(\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon E_2^2\right) \pi R_2^2 L_2 \\
& \Rightarrow E_1^2 R_1^2 L_1=E_2^2 R_2^2 L_2 \\
& \text { or } E_2=\frac{E_1 R_1}{R_2} \sqrt{\frac{L_1}{L_2}}=\frac{100 \mathrm{~d}}{(\mathrm{~d} / 2)} \sqrt{\frac{L_1}{L 1}}=200 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C} \\
& \qquad \quad\left[\because L_1=L_2=200 \mathrm{~cm}\right]
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ The amplitude of corresponding $E M$ wave is 200 N/C
or the wave is $E=200 \sin (\omega t-k x) \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$

questions.q: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave in free space is represented as $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}cos ( \omegat - kz ) \overset{^}{i}$. The corresponding magnetic induction vector will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}cos ( \omegat - kz ) \overset{^}{i}$:

Clearly, $( \omegat - kz )$ term represents, electromagnetic wave is travelling along $+ z$ direction or along $\overset{^}{k}$.

Now, in vector form, direction of electromagnetive wave is given by $\overset{^}{C} = \overset{^}{E} \times \overset{^}{B}$. Therefore, magnetic field is along $\overset{^}{j}$.

Also, we know that ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{C}$, where $C$ is speed of light.

Therefore, $\overset{→}{B} = \dfrac{E0}{C}cos ( \omegat - kz ) \overset{^}{j}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total average energy density of the electromagnetic field is given by, ${U}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}\left({E}_{0}\right)2$.

$⇒ {U}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12} \times \left(50\right)2$

$= 1 . 106 \times {10}^{– 8}Jm^{– 3}$

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave is propagating along the direction $\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}},$ with its polarization along the direction $\overset{^}{k .}$ The correct form of the magnetic field of the wave would be (here ${B}_{0}$ is an appropriate constant):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Polarization of EM Wave means Direction of Its electric Field

Electric field vector is along& $\overset{^}{k}$

So, unit electric filed vector,~$\overset{→}{E} = \overset{^}{k}$~(Given)

Direction of wave,$\overset{^}{c} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}$~ (Given)

$\overset{^}{B}$ denotes unit magnetic field vector.

$\overset{^}{B} = \overset{^}{C} \times \overset{^}{E}$

$\overset{^}{B} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2} \times \overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}}{2}$

General Form is~$B = ( {B}_{0}\overset{^}{B} ) cos \left(\omegat - \overset{^}{c}k\right)$

where~${B}_{0}$~is Magnitude of Magnetic Field

$So, B = ${B}_{0}\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}}{2}$cos \left(\omegat --k\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\right)$

questions.q: Which of the following Maxwell’s equation is valid for time varying conditions but not valid for static conditions:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maxwell’s four equations describe the electric and magnetic fields arising from distributions of electric charges and currents, and how those fields change in time.

The equations are as follows:

$∮ \overset{→}{E} \cdot d\overset{→}{A} = \dfrac{q}{ε0} . . . \left(1\right) ∮ \overset{⇀}{B} \cdot d\overset{⇀}{A} = 0 . . . \left(2\right) ∮ \overset{⇀}{E} \cdot d\overset{⇀}{l} = - \dfrac{∂ {ϕ}_{B}}{∂ t} . . . \left(3\right) ∮ \overset{⇀}{B} \cdotd\overset{⇀}{l} = {μ}_{0}I . . . \left(4\right)

From the above set of equations, it is clear that only the third equation is valid for time varying field.

Hence, this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by& $\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{i}  \left[cos \left($kz - \omegat\right)\right] + {B}_{1}\overset{^}{j}cos\left(kz + \omegat\right)$, where ${B}_{0} = 3 \times {10}^{– 5}T$ and ${B}_{1} = 2 \times {10}^{– 6}T$. The $RMS$~value of the force experienced by a stationary charge $Q = {10}^{– 4}C$ at $z = 0$ is closest to$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{i} \left[cos \left($kz - \omegat\right)\right] + {B}_{1}\overset{^}{j}cos\left(kz + \omegat\right)$
${B}_{0} = 3 \times {10}^{- 5}T \text{ and } {B}_{1} = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}T$
Electric filed associated with it is,
$\overset{→}{E} = - {B}_{0}c\overset{^}{j}cos \left(kz - \omegat\right) - {B}_{1}c\overset{^}{i}cos\left(kz + \omegat\right)$
Here, $c$ is~the speed of light in vacuum.
At $z = 0,$
${F}_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{\left(Q{B}_{0}c\right)}^{2} + {\left(Q{B}_{1}c\right)}^{2}}{2}}$
Here $c$ is speed of light in vacuum.
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{{\left({10}^{- 4} \times 3 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2} + {\left({10}^{- 4} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}\right)}^{2}}{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{0.81 + 0.0036}{2}} =0.6N

questions.q:
If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of $\frac{10}{\pi}$ and relative permittivity of $\frac{1}{0.0885}$, then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by ________ times.
\left(\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{H} / \mathrm{m}, \epsilon_0=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}\right.$
\left.\mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since velocity of light in terms of $\mu \ \text{ and } E$ is
$\begin{aligned}
& V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \epsilon}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \mu_r}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\epsilon_0 \epsilon_r}} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{r}} \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}} \\ & =\frac{C}{\sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{r}} \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}}=\frac{C}{\sqrt{\frac{10}{\pi} \times \frac{1}{0.0885}}} \\ & =\frac{C}{\sqrt{36}}=\frac{C}{6}
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{V} & =\frac{\mathrm{C}}{6} \\ \mathrm{C} & =6 \mathrm{~V}
\end{aligned}$
Velocity of light in vacuum is greater by 6 times the velocity of light in medium
Answer is 6

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $3GHz$ enters a dielectric medium of relative electric permittivity $2 . 25$ from vacuum. The wavelength of this wave in that medium will be _________~$\times {10}^{- 2}cm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda$ in vacuum~$= \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3 \times {10}^{9}} = 0 . 1m$

$∴ \lambda$ in medium $= \dfrac{0 . 1}{μ}$

Where refractive index

$\mu = \sqrt{{μ}_{r}{ε}_{r}}$

Assuming non-magnetic material~${μ}_{r} = 1$

$∴ \mu = \sqrt{2 . 25} = 1 . 5$

${λ}_{m} = \dfrac{0 . 1}{1 . 5} = \dfrac{1}{15}m = 6 . 67cm$

$= 667 \times {10}^{- 2}cm$
